Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording

05

“Was the night first or the day?”

Three explanations transmitted from ʿIkrima, Mujāhid ibn Jabr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk (Q 21:30).

631
Explanation from ʿIkrima No. 631: 6: 4

ʿIkrima

English
Transmission wording
631: 6:4. Sufyan, from Said ibn Masruq, from Ikrima, who said:
Ibn Abbas was asked, "Was the night first or the day?" He recited "Do those who disbelieve not see that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them," and then said, "Was there between them anything but darkness? That is so that they would know that the night came before the day" (verse 30).
العربية
631: 6: 4 سفيان عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ مَسْرُوقٍ عَنْ عكرمة قال سئل بن عَبَّاسٍ أَكَانَ اللَّيْلُ قَبْلُ أَوِ النهار فقرأ ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما ثُمَّ قَالَ هَلْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا ظُلْمَةٌ ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الليل قبل النهار (الآية 30) .

“when they were judging concerning the field”

An explanation transmitted from Masrūq (Q 21:78).

645
Explanation from Masrūq No. 645: 20: 18

Masrūq

English
Transmission wording
645: 20:18. Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Murra, from Masruq, on His words
"when they were judging concerning the field": He said, the field was grapes, "when the sheep of some people strayed into it": he said, at night ⦗p. 203⦘ He said: Dawud, peace be upon him, ruled that the sheep be handed over to them [the owners of the field]. Sulayman said, "What did Dawud say?" They said, "He handed the sheep over to them." He said, "If it were I, I would not hand them over, but I would let them [the field's owners] benefit from the sheep's wool, milk, and ghee, while the owners of the sheep tend the field until they restore it to what it was; then the sheep are returned to them and they return the field to its owners." So God, Mighty and Majestic, [gave understanding of it to] Sulayman (verse 78).

17

“Who will guarantee for me that he will not get angry, and he will be…”

An explanation transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith (Q 21:85).

646
Explanation from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith No. 646: 21: 28

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith

English
Transmission wording
646: 21:28. Sufyan, from al-Amash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said:
One of the prophets said, "Who will guarantee for me that he will not get angry, and he will be with me in my rank in Paradise?" A young man stood up and said, "I will." He said, "Sit down." Then he said it a second time, and that young man stood up and said, "I will." He said, "Sit him down." Then he said it a third time, and the young man stood up and said, "I will." He said, "Then it is well." He said: Then the prophet, peace be upon him, died, and he appointed the young man as his successor. He would judge between them and not become angry. Iblis schemed against him with everything to make him angry, but could not make him angry. One day, at midday, when he had finished judging between the people and had gone in to take a midday rest while fasting, [Iblis] came and knocked at his door. He sent a messenger with him, and he went with the messenger and then returned and said, "He did nothing at all about my need." He sent another messenger with him, who went and returned and said, "He did nothing at all about my need." So [the young man] took him by the hand and went off with him himself ⦗p. 204⦘ and when he was with him in the market, [Iblis] slipped away from him. He said: So he was named Dhu al-Kifl (verse 85).
العربية
646: 21: 28 سفيان عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ عَنِ الْمِنْهَالِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الحرث قَالَ كَانَ نَبِيٌّ مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ قَالَ مَنْ تَكَفَّلَ لِي بِأَنْ لا يغضب وهو مَعِي فِي دَرَجَتِي فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَقَامَ شَابٌّ فَقَالَ أَنَا فَقَالَ اقْعُدْ ثُمَّ قَالَ الثَّانِيَةَ فَقَامَ ذَلِكَ الشَّابُّ فَقَالَ أَنَا فَقَالَ أَقْعِدْهُ ثُمَّ قَالَهَا الثَّالِثَةَ فَقَامَ الشَّابُّ فَقَالَ أَنَا قَالَ فَنِعْمَ إِذًا قَالَ ثُمَّ مَاتَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ وَاسْتَخْلَفَ الشَّابَّ مَكَانَهُ فَكَانَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ وَلَا يَغْضَبُ فَاحْتَالَ لَهُ إِبْلِيسُ بكل شئ ليغضبه فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى أَنْ يُغْضِبَهُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ وَهُوَ نِصْفُ النَّهَارِ وَقَدْ فَرَغَ مِنْ قَضَائِهِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَدَخَلَ لِيُقَيِّلَ وَهُوَ صَائِمٌ أَتَاهُ فَدَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْبَابَ فَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ رَسُولًا فَذَهَبَ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَصْنَعْ فِي حَاجَتِي شيا فَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ رَسُولًا آخَرَ فَذَهَبَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَقَالَ لَمْ يَصْنَعْ في حاجتي شيا فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ وَبِنَفْسِهِ ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ ⦗p. 204⦘ مَعَهُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ مَعَهُ فِي السُّوقِ انْفَلَتَ مِنْهُ قَالَ فَسُمِّيَ ذا الكفل (الآية 85) .

24

“Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you…”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 21:101).

655
Explanation from Sufyān No. 655: 30: 23

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
655: 30:23. Sufyan said: When there was revealed
"Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will come to it," the polytheists argued with the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said, "Uzayr, Jesus, and the angels were worshipped, so are they in the Fire?" Then there was revealed: "Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it" (verse 101).
العربية
655: 30: 23 سفيان قال لما نزلت مع وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردن قَالَ خَاصَمَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فَقَالُوا فقد عبد عزيز وَعِيسَى وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ فَهُمْ فِي النَّارِ فَنَزَلَتْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَى أُولَئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ (الآية 101) .
